extracted.intended_audience: Contributors and code reviewers for the SageMath project (GitHub pull request authors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, reviewing, and managing pull requests (PRs) for inclusion in Sage, including the checks a reviewer must perform, criteria for accepting or rejecting PRs, and release-stage policies. Covers documentation, tests, conventions, and acceptable scope of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the GitHub checks
rubrics_metrics.description: We require all checks have passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reviewing, ensure all automated build/test/check workflows associated with the PR are green. A passing CI is a prerequisite for further manual review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the diff
rubrics_metrics.description: Click “Files changed” tab of the PR. Read through the changes of all modified files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pull request review tools to add comments directly to changed lines. Ensure you examine every modified file to understand the code changes and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test the code
rubrics_metrics.description: (This is optional if the build and test check has passed.) Checkout the code of the PR and run the relevant tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locally checkout the PR branch (or FETCH_HEAD) and run unit tests, doctests, or manual scenarios pertinent to the change. Manual testing is especially important for UI-related changes not covered by automated tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the code address the PR’s stated aim? Can it introduce any new problems? Does testing the new or fixed functionality with a variety of input, not just the examples in the documentation, give expected and robust output (and no unexpected errors or crashes)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the PR implements what it claims, doesn't produce regressions, and behaves robustly for varied inputs beyond the included examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: User documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the use of the new code clear to a user? Are all mathematical notions involved standard, or is there explanation (or a link to one) provided? Can the user find the new code easily if he/she needs it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check documentation strings, reference manual entries, tutorials, or example notebooks. Ensure explanations or references are provided for non-standard mathematical concepts and that docs point to where the feature lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the code sufficiently commented so that a developer does not have to wonder what exactly it does?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear inline comments, docstrings, and rationale for non-obvious implementation choices. Code should be understandable to future maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the code respect Sage’s conventions? Python’s conventions? Cython’s conventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify style, naming, API conventions, and project-specific expectations. Follow language best practices and Sage project conventions to maintain consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do all functions contain doctests? Use sage -coverage <files> to check it. Are all aspects of the new/modified methods and classes tested (see Writing testable examples)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submitted code includes doctests for behavior and edge cases. Use coverage tools to confirm tests exercise code paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bugfix doctest requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PR contains a bugfix, does it add a doctest illustrating that the bug has been fixed? This new doctest should contain the issue or PR number, for example See :issue:12345.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bugfix PRs must include a reproducible failing example as a doctest that demonstrates the bug and shows the fix; reference the original issue/PR in the doctest comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speedup claims must be demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the PR make any existing code slower? If the PR claims to speed up some computation, does the PR contain code examples to illustrate the claim? The PR should explain how the speedup is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks or illustrative examples should be included for performance claims; also check the change does not regress other code paths or inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build the manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reference manual build without errors (check both html and pdf)? See The Sage Manuals to learn how to build the manuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt or verify successful builds of documentation artifacts; ensure sphinx/reST sources do not cause build failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look at the manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reference manual look okay? The changes may have typos that allow the documentation to build without apparent errors but that may cause badly formatted output or broken hyperlinks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect rendered docs for formatting issues, broken links, bad typesetting, or misleading wording introduced by the PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run the tests (full scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do all doctests pass without errors? Unrelated components of Sage may be affected by the change. Check all tests in the whole library, including “long” doctests (this can be done with make ptestlong) and any optional doctests related to the functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform broad test runs where appropriate; for UI changes prefer manual Jupyter-based testing. Ensure unrelated parts of the library are not broken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review status outcomes and when to set them
rubrics_metrics.description: positive review: If the answers to the questions above and other reasonable questions are “yes”, you can set the PR to positive review status. needs work: If something is not as it should, write a list of all points that need to be addressed and change the PR’s status to needs work. needs info: If something is not clear and prevents you from going further, ask your question and set the PR’s status to needs info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PR status mechanism to communicate review decisions clearly, and provide actionable feedback or specific questions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unsure how to conclude a review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not know what to do, for instance if you don’t feel experienced enough to take a final decision, explain what you already did in a comment and ask if someone else could take a look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the checks you performed and where you stopped; request targeted assistance from more experienced reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of reviews — 'The perfect is the enemy of the good'
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of the review is to ensure that the Sage code guidelines are followed and that the implementation is mathematically correct. Please refrain from additional feature requests or open-ended discussion about alternative implementations. If you want the code written differently, your suggestion should be a clear and actionable request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit reviews to correctness, adherence to guidelines, and actionable improvements. Avoid broad stylistic debates or speculative redesigns unless they are necessary and concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs: One Issue Per One Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue must cover only one issue and should not be a laundry list of unrelated issues. If an issue covers more than one issue, we cannot close it and while some of the patches have been applied to a given release, the issue would remain in limbo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit focused issues/PRs; split unrelated changes into separate tickets or PRs to allow independent review and closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs: No Patch Bombs
rubrics_metrics.description: Code that goes into Sage is peer-reviewed. If you show up with 80,000 lines of code bundle that completely rips out a subsystem and replaces it with something else, you can imagine that the review process will be a little tedious. These huge patch bombs are problematic for several reasons and we prefer small, gradual changes that are easy to review and apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer incremental, well-scoped changes. Large, wholesale replacements should be avoided unless unavoidable; if unavoidable, prepare maintainers for the scope and plan for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs: Sage Specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage’s philosophy is that we ship everything (or close to it) in one source tarball to make debugging possible. Once you start replacing some of the more essential components of Sage that are commonly packaged (e.g. Pari, GAP, lisp, gmp), it is no longer a problem that belongs in our tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the problem lies in an external packaged dependency, file a bug report with that package’s maintainers rather than in Sage’s tracker; ensure PRs are appropriate for the Sage codebase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs: No Support Discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: GitHub is not meant to be a system to track down problems when using Sage. An issue should be clearly a bug and not 'I tried to do X and I couldn’t get it to work. How do I do this?' That is usually not a bug in Sage and it is likely that sage-support can answer that question for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve the issue tracker for reproducible bugs and actionable development tasks; direct usage/support questions to user support channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs: Solution Must Be Achievable
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues must be achievable. Many times, issues that fall into this category usually ran afoul to some of the other rules listed above. An example would be to 'Make Sage the best CAS in the world'. There is no metric to measure this properly and it is highly subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame issues with concrete, achievable goals and acceptance criteria. Avoid vague, unmeasurable objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: All code must be peer-reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: All code that goes into Sage is peer-reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No code should be merged without review by other developers; the review should focus on the checklist items described (tests, docs, conventions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Release process: Beta Release Stage merging policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For preparing a new beta release or the first release candidate, all positively reviewed PRs with the forthcoming release milestone are considered. The Release Manager merges PRs in batches of 10 to 20 PRs. If a merge conflict of a PR to the Release Manager’s branch occurs, the PR is set back to 'needs work' status. Each batch of merged PRs undergoes integration testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that their PR may be merged in batches and may be set back to needs work if conflicts or integration issues arise. Mark appropriate release milestone to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release process: Release Candidate Stage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first release candidate has been made, the project is in the release candidate stage, and a modified procedure is used. Now only PRs with a priority set to 'blocker' are considered. PRs with all other priorities, including 'critical', are ignored. Hence if a ticket is important enough to merit inclusion in this stage, it should be set to 'blocker' by adding p: blocker / 1 label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set priorities correctly; only genuine blockers with documented rationale will be considered for inclusion in later release candidate batches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocker PR guidance and rationale requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Blocker PRs: The goal of the release process is to make a stable release of high quality. Be aware that there is a risk/benefit trade-off in merging a PR. The benefit of merging a PR is the improvement that the PR brings, such as fixing a bug. However, any code change has a risk of introducing unforeseen new problems and thus delaying the release: If a new issue triggers another release candidate, it can delay the release by up to 2 weeks. Hence developers should use 'blocker' priority sparingly and should indicate the rationale on the PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who request blocker status must explain why the PR is essential now; feature PRs and large refactors are usually not blockers. Provide clear reasoning on the PR for any blocker request.
